abstract.t: This document specifies DNS for AI Discovery (DNS-AID), a method for publishing AI agents in the Domain Name System (DNS) so that other agents can discover them. It defines three discovery use cases, ordered by increasing latency and computational cost. In the known- agent case, the requestor knows both the agent and its domain, and a single DNS query returns connectivity information and key metadata. In the known-organization case, the requestor knows the domain but not which agent provides a required capability, and queries a well- known organizational index to get connectivity information to enable a capability search of a catalog, agent registry or database. In the known-capability case, the requestor knows only the required capability and must rely on an external directory or search service. This document addresses the known-agent and known-organization cases. The known-capability case is out of scope, but search and cataloging services can be built from the organizational index defined here. Once a client has learned an organization’s agents, later interactions can use the known-agent case, relying on a minimal, cacheable record set that each organization controls. DNS-AID uses Service Binding (SVCB) records, optionally with DNS-Based Service Discovery (DNS-SD) labels, DNSSEC, and DANE TLSA records. This gives agents direct connections that no third party mediates and works the same way on public and private networks. No new resource record types, opcodes, or response codes are introduced.
